QuestionStmt.S: The value of $\sqrt{3} \cot 20^\circ - 4 \cos 20^\circ$ is equal to

Solution.S:
We have:

$$\sqrt{3} \cot 20^\circ - 4 \cos 20^\circ = \sqrt{3} \frac{\cos 20^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ} - 4 \cos 20^\circ$$

$$= \frac{\sqrt{3} \cos 20^\circ - 4 \sin 20^\circ \cos 20^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ}$$

$$= \frac{\sqrt{3} \cos 20^\circ - 2 \cdot 2 \sin 20^\circ \cos 20^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3} \cos 20^\circ - 2 \sin 40^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ}$$

Using $\sqrt{3} = 2 \sin 60^\circ$:

$$= \frac{2 \sin 60^\circ \cos 20^\circ - 2 \sin 40^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ} = 2 \cdot \frac{\sin 60^\circ \cos 20^\circ - \sin 40^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ}$$

Using $2 \sin A \cos B = \sin(A+B) + \sin(A-B)$:

$$2 \sin 60^\circ \cos 20^\circ = \sin 80^\circ + \sin 40^\circ$$

Thus numerator becomes $\sin 80^\circ + \sin 40^\circ - 2 \sin 40^\circ = \sin 80^\circ - \sin 40^\circ$.

Now $\sin 80^\circ - \sin 40^\circ = 2 \cos 60^\circ \sin 20^\circ = 2 \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot \sin 20^\circ = \sin 20^\circ$.

Therefore the expression becomes:

$$\frac{\sin 20^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ} = 1$$

Thus the correct option is A: 1.
